components.css: .ds-proc{position:relative;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(4,minmax(0,1fr));gap:12px;align-items:end;height:112px;margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;}.ds-proc::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:14px;height:3px;background:var(--ink, #2a2724);border-radius:9999px;}.ds-st{--lift:0;position:relative;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:flex-end;height:100%;}.ds-card{position:relative;z-index:1;width:100%;max-width:108px;padding:8px 6px;border-radius:2px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:4px;background:var(--pulp-2, #e8e0d2);color:var(--ink-2, #4a443d);font-family:'Archivo Narrow', Courier Prime, ui-monospace, monospace;font-weight:600;font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.08em;text-transform:uppercase;transform:translateY(calc(-30px - 12px * var(--lift)));box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(42,39,36,.2),4px 8px 14px -8px rgba(42,39,36,.35);transition:transform 700ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1),background-color 300ms,color 300ms,box-shadow 700ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1);}.ds-card small{font-family:Courier Prime,system-ui,sans-serif;font-weight:400;text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;opacity:.8;}.ds-pin{position:absolute;bottom:14px;width:3px;height:calc(30px + 12px * var(--lift));background:var(--ink-2, #4a443d);border-radius:9999px;transition:height 700ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1);}.ds-joint{position:absolute;bottom:9px;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--pulp, #f2ece1);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 2.5px var(--ink, #2a2724);}.ds-done .ds-card{background:var(--pulp, #f2ece1);color:var(--forest, #3f6a3a);}.ds-near{--lift:.2;}.ds-run{--lift:1;}.ds-run .ds-card{background:var(--crimson, #b3262d);color:var(--pulp, #f2ece1);transform:translateY(-42px) rotate(-2deg);box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(42,39,36,.2),10px 22px 24px -8px rgba(42,39,36,.6);}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-card,.ds-pin{transition:none;}}

narrative.overview:
CodeBase is built as a kinetic paper automaton sitting on a sheet of kraft board. One crank turns a repository through its linkage (clone, parse, extract, graph, embed, store, answer), and whichever stage is moving lifts off the rail, turns crimson and folds open to show what it actually produced. Everything else is cut paper: pulp-white sheets slotted into the board, cut folder tabs, paper strips for buttons, charcoal ink plates for code. The world is warm, physical and matte; depth comes from paper lifting off board, never from glow.

Density follows the job. The home page is spacious and persuasive (one machine, one claim, four measured figures). The workstation is a dense tool: a sticky paper-tab nav, a repository strip, a row of nine numbered folder tabs, and one large paper sheet per tool. The system refuses the dark dev-tool dashboard it replaced: no glowing cards, no gradient text, no icon tiles, no indigo.

The machine only shows what is real. Figures are live from the index API or measured in `evals_report.json`; anything drawn by hand says so on the page.
keyCharacteristics: Kraft board ground with fibre grain; pulp paper pieces with soft cast shadows and slot marks.
One moving colour: crimson marks the active tab, running stage, primary action and the failure or critical finding that stops the machine.
Matrixtype Display as die-cut letterpress caps; Archivo Narrow caps for every tab, label and button strip; Courier Prime typewriter face for body, code and every figure.
The Procession: stage cards pinned by linkage pins to one ink rail, reused on home, indexing and the chat agent pipeline.
Crank motion: 700ms on `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`; stages unfold from their top crease.
Near-square corners (2px strips, 3px sheets); cut shoulders on tabs.

rules.name: The Crimson Moves Rule
rules.body: Crimson belongs only to what is moving or has stopped the machine: the active tab, the running stage, the primary action, the critical finding, the error. A static decoration never gets it. If two crimson things compete in one view, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Printed Ink Rule
rules.body: Forest, ochre and rust are state, never decoration. Each is used as a wash plus a 35% inset outline, or as a solid lamp.

rules.name: The Board Text Rule
rules.body: Text set directly on kraft uses ink or board ink only; ash and paper greys are for text on paper.

rules.name: The Figures Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Every number is Courier Prime (or Matrixtype at display scale) with tabular figures; inline code sits on a pulp chip, since body and code share one face.

rules.name: The Caps Are Condensed Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text is Archivo Narrow with positive tracking, or Matrixtype Display. Courier Prime is never set in caps.

rules.name: The Lift Means Selected Rule
rules.body: A piece rises (translateY and a deeper shadow) when it is hovered, selected or running; at rest it stays down. The Procession's shadow grows with each card's lift.

rules.name: The Slot Rule
rules.body: Major sheets (the crank stage, repository strip, closing call) are tabbed into the board with two dark kraft slot marks at the side edges. Slots are for sheets that anchor a view, not for every card.

dos: Do keep crimson for what is moving or has stopped the machine: active tab, running stage, primary action, critical finding, error.
Do build every surface from the paper pieces: sheet (3px, Lift 2), flat paper (2px, inset rule), ink plate for code, strip labels in Semi Condensed caps.
Do make buttons paper strips; give the one primary action per view the crimson strip with its eyelet rivet.
Do show pipelines with the Procession on one ink rail, and move them on the 700ms crank ease.
Do unfold new stage content from its top crease when the stage changes, and let reduced motion switch it in place.
Do set every figure in mono with tabular numbers, and take it live from the index API or from `evals_report.json`; keep the weak scores in.
Do label anything drawn by hand on the page itself ("Sample diagram drawn by hand, not generated from this index", "values illustrative", "Example").
donts: Don't invent numbers, customers, testimonials or usage figures; the old parse-integrity, latency and context-size figures must not return.
Don't present a sample or illustrative diagram as generated output.
Don't use crimson as decoration, and don't use forest, ochre or rust outside state.
Don't bring back the dark indigo dashboard: glowing cards, gradient text, icon tiles, glassmorphism.
Don't round paper beyond 3px or turn tags into rounded pills; circles are for pins, knobs, rivets and lamps only.
Don't set ash or grey text directly on kraft.
